facts.text: The Athens metro is modern, cheap, and directly connects the airport to the city center — a noticeably better value and faster option than a taxi for solo/light-luggage travelers.

A taverna meal (moussaka, souvlaki, Greek salad) for two with a modest amount of wine typically runs €25-40 outside the most touristy zones — genuinely one of the cheaper major European capitals for eating well.

Restaurants with staff calling out to passersby directly around the Acropolis Museum and Plaka's main tourist strip are reliably pricier and lower quality than a few streets into Plaka's quieter lanes or nearby Psyrri.
The Acropolis is dramatically less crowded at opening time (early morning) than midday, especially in summer heat — both a comfort and a crowd consideration.
Summer heat in Athens is intense (regularly 35°C+/95°F+ July-August) — many locals and savvy visitors avoid strenuous sightseeing between roughly 1-5pm.

Greek cuisine has strong inherent vegetarian/vegan options (dips, vegetable dishes, legumes) even at traditional tavernas, unlike many other traditional European cuisines that require more deliberate seeking.
